workflow.title: Follow the workflow from preview through verified result
steps: Check the live service state and command catalog before proposing a state change.
Request a preview, present its revision and source binding, and wait for separate trusted host approval before execution.
Observe the returned job and verify its published native artifact, units, independent reference, and requested business outcome.
workflow.success: Report completion only after host job evidence and native artifact checks support the requested outcome.
workflow.recovery: For an unknown submission outcome, query the original execution identity and do not retry automatically. Stop when the source binding or artifact evidence changes.

project.title: Inspect linked project and document state
steps: Use the host project catalog to identify linked documents, accepted revisions, and available snapshots.
Keep FE source identity, independent reference data, and caller-provided data as separate claims; retain their hashes and revisions.
Treat a project snapshot as available only when the host reports its binding and verification state.
project.success: The selected document and revision are identified by host-owned project metadata.
project.recovery: If a document is missing, dirty, stale, or ambiguous, refresh the catalog and ask the caller to resolve the source before proceeding.

model.source.title: Register or inspect a trusted model source
steps: Use the live operation schema and source catalog to select an explicit source binding.
Register sources only through the trusted owner path and preserve the returned source identity and content hash.
Before a solve, confirm the selected source still matches the accepted project revision.
model.source.success: The host reports a stable source identity tied to the inspected bytes and current project state.
model.source.recovery: If the source changes or its owner binding cannot be verified, stop and re-register through the trusted owner workflow.

result.title: Inspect a published result artifact
steps: Select a result from the actual job and artifact catalog, then keep that identity fixed while reading pages or channels.
Check reported units, time coverage, node or channel identity, and source-job binding before interpreting values.
Compare FE results with an independent reference and assess the caller's business criteria separately.
result.success: Every reported value is tied to the selected published artifact and retains its declared units and scope.
result.recovery: If pagination, artifact identity, units, or source binding changes, discard the partial comparison and query the catalog again.

native.title: Use native document operations with explicit bindings
steps: Read the native operation descriptor and its current source, revision, and unit context.
Preview edits before applying them, and keep the native document identity separate from imported or caller-supplied references.
After execution, inspect the published native artifact and verify the requested engineering outcome independently.
native.success: The operation returns an artifact bound to the intended native document and its accepted revision.
native.recovery: On a revision conflict or stale source, refresh the document and create a new preview only after reconciling the changed state.

extension.title: Use extensions only in the host's declared trust mode
steps: Check the live extension runtime flags; the normal mode keeps trusted extension execution disabled.
Use trusted developer mode only when the host explicitly enables it, and review bundle validation and declared inputs before activation.
Treat the extension runtime as trusted code execution; the runtime flags do not claim an operating-system sandbox.
extension.success: An extension result is accepted only when the host reports its validated version, runtime binding, and result checks.
extension.recovery: If trust mode is disabled, validation fails, or an extension outcome is uncertain, stop and preserve the candidate and validation record.

task.plan.title: Build a bounded plan from the live tool catalog
steps: Use only operations and commands present in the current host catalog, with each node's live schema and declared dependencies.
Request previews for state-changing nodes and obtain separate trusted approval for each required node before submission.
Bound model calls, tool calls, active time, and deadlines; verify each job, native artifact, units, and business criterion from host evidence.
task.plan.success: Plan progress follows host-observed node results, and completion requires verified evidence for every required node.
task.plan.recovery: Pause on unknown submissions, missing evidence, or exhausted budgets. Reconcile the original job identity; never invent a successful exit result or resubmit blindly.

task.node.title: Advance a task node from trusted evidence
steps: Keep the node's plan, attempt, source, and capability bindings unchanged while work is in flight.
Use host-observed query results for read-only nodes and a fresh preview plus separate approval for each command node.
Accept completion only from the host's verified job, native artifact, unit, and business checks.
task.node.success: The node reaches a terminal success state only after its declared predicate is satisfied by trusted host evidence.
task.node.recovery: On a lost response or binding conflict, pause and reconcile the same attempt. Do not convert missing output or a process exit code into a fabricated success.

schema.title: Use the runtime schema as the operation contract
steps: Read the exact schema and precondition from the live operation or command descriptor.
Use this guidance only for human workflow steps; do not copy parameter rules from prose or add fields absent from the runtime schema.
Bind the guidance to the returned schema hash and catalog hash before presenting it.
schema.success: The operation is interpreted using its current runtime signature, units, and preconditions.
schema.recovery: If a descriptor or schema hash changes, discard the old interpretation and query capabilities again.

knowledge.title: Treat knowledge as guidance, not a capability source
steps: Search only guidance attached to operations and commands present in the current runtime catalog.
Use the item hashes and source path to identify the packaged guidance version.
Keep approval and execution decisions in the separate trusted host workflow.
knowledge.success: A knowledge result explains a catalogued capability without adding permissions or changing its schema.
knowledge.recovery: If a capability has no matching rule, stop and report the coverage gap; do not infer an operation or retry an unknown identifier.

telemetry.title: Read telemetry as bounded observation
steps: Read only the channels and time window reported for the selected job.
Preserve sequence, timestamps, and declared units when comparing samples or exporting data.
Use telemetry as evidence about an observed run, not as a command or substitute for artifact verification.
telemetry.success: Samples remain tied to the job, channel, and time range that the host returned.
telemetry.recovery: If sequence or job identity changes, resume from a fresh host query and keep incomplete observations marked as partial.

audit.title: Inspect audit history as diagnostic evidence
steps: Read audit entries in revision order and retain the operation and job identities they reference.
Use audit records to explain state transitions while checking result artifacts through their dedicated interfaces.
Do not treat an audit entry by itself as proof that an engineering goal was met.
audit.success: The reported history matches host revisions and does not expose approval tokens or other credentials.
audit.recovery: If revisions are missing or inconsistent, query from the last confirmed revision and report the gap.

jobs.title: Observe the original job through its terminal state
steps: Poll the same host-issued job identity and distinguish queued, active, and terminal states.
After completion, inspect the associated native artifact and its unit-aware result evidence.
Use explicit cancellation or recovery operations only when their live preconditions are met.
jobs.success: A job is reported complete only when the host marks it terminal and the required result checks pass.
jobs.recovery: For an interrupted or uncertain job, reconcile its original attempt and preserve its history; do not create a duplicate job automatically.

execution.title: Reconcile an uncertain execution without retrying
steps: Query execution using the identity from the original preview or submission.
Treat a missing receipt as unknown until the host confirms the outcome.
Continue only after reconciling the same request, job, and source bindings.
execution.success: The original request resolves to its host receipt and job identity, or remains explicitly unaccepted.
execution.recovery: Never retry an unknown execution automatically. Preserve the original request identity and ask the trusted host to reconcile it.

rules.title: Inspect the live workflow capabilities
steps: Read the current operation and command catalog before choosing a call.
Use each entry's runtime schema and precondition as the operation contract.
Bind selected guidance to the live catalog hash and exact schema hash.
rules.success: The selected ID is present in the current catalog and its exact descriptor is available.
rules.recovery: If an ID or schema is absent, refresh capabilities and stop; do not invent an operation or command.

rules.title: Preview a proposed state change
steps: Request a preview against the current project revision and explicit source binding.
Review the normalized effects and preview hash with the caller.
Keep preview separate from execution and wait for the trusted host's approval step.
rules.success: The host returns a preview bound to the reviewed request; a preview does not execute it.
rules.recovery: On a stale revision or source conflict, refresh the project state and reconcile before requesting a new preview.

rules.title: Submit only a separately approved preview
steps: Execute only the exact preview after separate trusted host approval for that preview hash.
Treat the accepted response as job submission and observe the host-issued job identity.
Verify the native artifact, declared units, independent reference, and caller's business goal before reporting completion.
rules.success: The host accepts the approved preview and provides an execution receipt or job identity for verification.
rules.recovery: If the response is lost or uncertain, query execution by the original preview hash; never submit a second execution blindly.
